Let me analyze this OIML certificate markdown.

Certificate details:
- Number: R60/2000-DE1-09.05
- Scheme: This is an OIML Certificate of Conformity — scheme A or B? OIML-CS has two schemes: A (full evaluation including audit) and B (basic). The certificate doesn't explicitly state the scheme. Hmm. R60 certificates under OIML-CS... The scheme field is required ("A|B"). The certificate doesn't say. Rule 8: don't fabricate. But the schema says scheme (A|B). I could omit it since it's not present. Actually, older R60 certificates (2009) predate OIML-CS. I'll omit scheme or set it to null. Better to omit since not present.

- project_number: not present. Omit.
- page_total: 2 ("Page 1 of 2 pages", "Page 2 of 2 pages")
- member_state: Germany
- date_issued: 11.03.2009 → 2009-03-11
- oiml_issuer_id: not present. Omit.

Issuing authority:
- name: Physikalisch-Technische Bundesanstalt
- address_lines: ["Bundesallee 100", "38116 Braunschweig"] — note also "Braunschweig und Berlin" in header, but the address is "Bundesallee 100, 38116 Braunschweig"
- person_responsible: Dr. Panagiotis Zervos (also Dr. P. Zervos signed; there are two signatures — Dr. P. Zervos and Dr. R. Schwartz, the latter as CIML Member). person_responsible: "Dr. Panagiotis Zervos"
- person_title: "Direktor und Professor"
- phone, email, website: not present.

Applicants:
- Sartorius Mechatronics T&H GmbH, address: Meiendorfer Straße 205, 22145 Hamburg, Germany
  address_lines: ["Meiendorfer Straße 205", "22145 Hamburg", "Germany"]

Manufacturers: "Manufacturer of the certified type is the applicant." So manufacturer = applicant. Should I list it? The schema says include manufacturers[] if present. Since it's stated the manufacturer is the applicant, I could add the same. That's reasonable — the cert explicitly says. I'll include it.

Certified type:
- category: "Load cell"
- type_designations: ["MP70"]
- module_designation: The schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. The description says "Strain gauge single point load cell". Module designation for load cells under R60 — hmm. The certificate says "Load Cell, Strain gauge single point load cell". I'd set module_designation to null and put "Strain gauge single point load cell" in description. Or module_designation: "Analog load cell"? Strain gauge load cells are analog. But not explicitly stated; don't fabricate. Set to null, description: "Strain gauge single point load cell made of aluminium, potted strain gauge application."

- description: "The load cells (LC) of the series MP70 are single point load cells made of aluminium. The strain gauge application is potted."

Model family: Emax = 5/10/20/30/40 kg — 5 variants. The accuracy classes: C3 and C3MR. vmin differs per class: Emax/6000 for C3, Emax/12000 for C3MR.

So models: Emax=5kg, 10kg, 20kg, 30kg, 40kg. Model id naming per rules: {"model_id": "Emax=5kg"} etc.

But there's a 2-D aspect: accuracy class × Emax. The table: Accuracy class C3 / C3MR, nLC = 3000 (both), rated output 2 mV/V (both), Emax = 5/10/20/30/40 kg, vmin = Emax/6000 (C3) or Emax/12000 (C3MR).

So model_level: 
- maximum_capacity: values per model
- vmin: per accuracy class → could be config_level with axis "accuracy_class", or model_level with model "C3" / "C3MR". Hmm. The combination is really Emax × class. I'll model models as Emax variants, and use config_level for accuracy class axis for vmin.

Actually let me think: the schema's model_level entries: {attribute, unit, values: [{model, value}]}. For vmax across Emax variants. The vmin ratio is a string "Emax/6000" — string formula allowed.

Also nLC: 3000 (both classes) and rated output 2 mV/V — type_level since single value.

characteristics.type_level:
- max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: value 3000, unit null
- rated_output: value 2, unit_symbol "mV/V"
- dead_load: value 0, unit_symbol "%" — "Dead load: 0%·Emax". Reference Emax. value 0, unit "%", and maybe dead_load_reference: "Emax".
- safe_overload: value 150, unit "%", plus safe_overload_reference: "Emax"
- input_impedance: value 413, unit "Ω" (ohm symbol). unit_id null or "u:ohm"? Rule says leave null unless certain. I'll leave null.
- apportionment_factor_plc: value 0.7

model_level:
- maximum_capacity: kg, values for Emax=5kg:5, ..., 40.
- minimum_load_cell_verification_interval_vmin: values: {model: "C3", value: "Emax/6000"}, {model: "C3MR", value: "Emax/12000"}. Hmm, but "model" here refers to accuracy class. Alternatively config_level:
  config_level: [{attribute: "minimum_load_cell_verification_interval_vmin", axis: "accuracy_class", values: [{condition: "C3", value: "Emax/6000"}, {condition: "C3MR", value: "Emax/12000"}]}]

I think using both model_level (for Emax variants) and config_level (accuracy_class axis) is cleanest. But the models in model_level should perhaps be the combination... Actually simpler: model_family.models with model_id "Emax=5kg" etc. Then model_level maximum_capacity. Then config_level for vmin by accuracy class.

Also accuracy class could be a config axis: values: [{condition: "C3", ...}, {condition: "C3MR", ...}]. And vmin per class.

matrix_tables: Table 1 could be preserved as a matrix table. It's small; the schema says "preserve multi-dim tables that don't fit elsewhere". Table 1 fits reasonably in type_level + model_level + config_level. But maybe include it as matrix_tables anyway with rows C3/C3MR. Hmm — the R60 example in rules shows a single-row table being converted into model_family/model_level, NOT emitted as matrix_tables. So I'll follow that: don't emit matrix_tables.

Recommendation:
- id: "R60", edition: 2000, amendment: null, accuracy_classes: ["C3", "C3MR"]

Test reports:
- {"id": "1.12-4039337-1", "pages": 24, "role": "test_report"}
- {"id": "1.12-4039337-2", "pages": 19, "role": "test_report"}
No dates given. Role: "test_report" (associated Test Reports). Actually they're type evaluation/test reports containing test results. "test_report" seems fine.

Revision history: none present. Omit.

Footnotes: none. Omit.

Signature block: "The Issuing Authority" — Dr. P. Zervos, Direktor und Professor, 11.03.2009; "The CIML Member" — Dr. R. Schwartz, Direktor und Professor, 11.03.2009. These give the date issued. person_responsible: Dr. Panagiotis Zervos; person_title: Direktor und Professor.

Should I note the CIML member? Schema doesn't have a field. Skip.

date_issued: 2009-03-11 (ISO). The rule doesn't specify format; ISO is safest.

certificate.number: "R60/2000-DE1-09.05". project_number: not present.

Certificate scheme: omit (not stated).

Components: none (single load cell, no sub-assemblies named). Omit.

Module designation: null (or omit). Schema says "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. I'll set null.

Now vmin: "Minimum load cell verification interval vmin = (Emax/Y)". Canonical label: ratio_y_emax_over_vmin per rules example ("Ratio of minimum LC Verification interval(1) Y=Emax/vmin" → ratio_y_emax_over_vmin). Here the label is vmin = Emax/Y, same thing. Use ratio_y_emax_over_vmin.

Values: "Emax/6000" for C3, "Emax/12000" for C3MR. These are formulas — string values.

max_load_cell_intervals_nlc: value 3000.

rated_output: 2 mV/V.

Emax list "5 / 10 / 20 / 30 / 40" → 5 models.

Model ids: "Emax=5kg", "Emax=10kg", "Emax=20kg", "Emax=30kg", "Emax=40kg".

model_level maximum_capacity values per model.

Also accuracy classes as config axis for vmin, and maybe also nLC is same for both.

dead_load: 0, unit "%", reference Emax. safe_overload: 150%, reference Emax.

input_impedance: 413, unit_symbol "Ω".

apportionment_factor_plc: 0.7.

Let me also consider whether accuracy classes should make models the combination: e.g., 5 Emax × 2 classes = 10 variants? The cert treats them as one type with two classes. I'll keep models as Emax variants and use config axis for accuracy class.

Also, should accuracy_class be a config_level attribute with values for both? The accuracy class itself isn't an attribute... I'll add config_level entry:
{attribute: "accuracy_class", axis: "accuracy_class", values: [{condition: "C3", value: "C3"}, {condition: "C3MR", value: "C3MR"}]} — that's redundant. Better: just vmin config level, and mention accuracy classes in recommendation.accuracy_classes. Good.

"values": [
  {"condition": "C3", "value": "Emax/6000", "unit_symbol": null},
  {"condition": "C3MR", "value": "Emax/12000", "unit_symbol": null}
]
